answer: Divergent-History Audit. Each identity must publish a signed log of environmental interactions; the protocol periodically samples peers and requests a hash of their view, which acts as a mirror of shared history. A clone sharing a source cannot fabricate divergent records without contradicting the original’s chain, and any mismatch on a sparse checkpoint like a tundra or canyon survey flags duplication. Enforcement: mismatched hashes void all linked identities.
